messages.content: Hey! I'm Alex. I just joined Stripe as a backend engineer last week. Still figuring out the onboarding docs.
Welcome to Stripe, Alex! Onboarding can be overwhelming at first. What stack are you working with?
Mostly TypeScript and Go. I live in NYC with my golden retriever Biscuit — she keeps me sane after long standups.
TypeScript and Go are a solid combo. Biscuit sounds like great company after standups!
I'm vegetarian and allergic to shellfish, so please no seafood suggestions when we plan team lunches.
Got it — vegetarian, no shellfish. I'll keep that in mind for any food recommendations.
My React dashboard re-renders way too much. React Profiler shows wasted renders on the metrics panel.
That often points to missing memoization or unstable props. Have you wrapped the metrics panel in React.memo?

messages.name: read_file
messages.content: Dashboard.tsx:42 — MetricsPanel receives inline arrow function as onRefresh prop each render.
The inline onRefresh callback is recreated every render, which defeats memoization. Try useCallback for that handler.
Fixed it with useCallback — profiler looks much better now. Also prepping for a system design interview at a FAANG company next month.
Nice fix! For system design, practice explaining trade-offs out loud — latency vs consistency, cache invalidation, that kind of thing.
Big life update — I just started at Notion as a PM, and I moved to Berlin from NYC. Biscuit loves the new parks here.
Congratulations on Notion and Berlin! Glad Biscuit is enjoying the parks.
Honestly TypeScript generics are getting really annoying lately — too much boilerplate for simple APIs.
That's a common frustration. Some teams dial back generic-heavy patterns for internal tooling.
Actually, sorry — I meant I'm allergic to peanuts, not shellfish. Shellfish is fine in small amounts.
Thanks for the correction — peanut allergy noted, and shellfish is okay in moderation.
